Obamacare premiums are going up 25 percent. So what happens next?

the ACA implodes, or the government ratchets up fines to a point at which debtors prisons become a thing again.

First, you need to understand WHY premiums are jumping 25% (in some cases 100+%) - insurance profits are capped, by law... 80% of all income must be spent on patient care. the remaining 20% of income has to cover administrative costs, IT, Infrastructure, employee salaries, and yes, profit. Prior to the ACA, Health Insurance companies were able to "balance" their outgoing healthcare expenditures by ensuring that they had significantly more healthy people (no cost subscribers) than sick people. Often, exceedingly sick people, or people requiring lifelong, continual care would have to either pay MORE for insurance (since they would be using more) or were denied entirely (since the cost of providing care would be detrimental to the group as a whole). The ACA made this practice illegal.

The tradeoff was supposed to be that by requiring all the fit, healthy, young people to buy into insurance plans (or pay a fine!), that it would offset the huge cost of the previously "uninsurable" millions.

This is a great lesson in risk economics. You cannot force people to buy something they don't want or need. Given the choice between a few hundred dollar fine or thousands in premium costs, a healthy, millennial or GenX-er isn't wrong to gamble on the system, pay the fine and save money. Or, just reduce your tax withholding, skip getting a refund every year (which you should do anyways. why "loan" the government money, interest free) and tell Washington to go fly a kite (ACA "penalties" can only be taken from your tax refund checks - they cannot send you a bill)

The end result is the Insurance companies are struggling under the weight (teehee) of the unhealthy masses. The law leaves them no choice but to continually increase premium costs (since "profit" and expenses are a fixed value) to ensure that all the customers get their care paid for. Faced with this, many insurance providers are simply dropping out of the market entirely (39 states now only have ONE aca provider).

Here's the real stinker - Everyone thinks that the ACA was a healthcare law. It's not. It's a Health Insurance law. It doesn't do anything to regulate drug costs, quality of care, medical tort reform, service fees at providers, non-payment policies, DME costs, loopholes in non-profit healthcare, or allow collective bargaining by the largest health insurance provider in the country (Medicare).

All the ACA does is mandate that you hand your money over to a third party that gets to make all of your healthcare decisions without you.
Next, congress will vote to subsidise those who can't afford the higher premiums, which the fed has been doing. Hint: This was the plan from the start. A gigantic welfare program.
